BiblicalUsage: Chariysh is ploughing, or its season, and it marks the farmer's year. Six days thou shalt work, but on the seventh day thou shalt rest: in earing time and in harvest thou shalt rest. Joseph tells his brothers five years remain in which there shall neither be earing nor harvest, and Samuel warns that a king will set men to ear his ground and reap his harvest.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the ploughing season is the Bible's picture of ordinary work under God's ordering: even in earing time and harvest, the Sabbath stands. Joseph's famine took away both earing and harvest, and Samuel's king would take the ploughmen for himself. I hold that work is God's gift, and rest is His command, and neither may swallow the other.
